newsitem.title: BRAZIL: THREE BANKS TO BID FOR BRAZIL'S CREDIREAL.
newsitem.headline: THREE BANKS TO BID FOR BRAZIL'S CREDIREAL.

text.p: Three financial institutions are due to bid at Thursday's auction of Minas Gerais state bank Credireal, the second Brazilian state-owned bank due to be privatized, state officials said.

Banco Industrial e Comercial (Bicbanco), Companhia de Investimentos Latinoamericana and Varejo S.A. Participacao e Administracao were the only bidders out of eight prequalified investors which presented financial guarantees allowing them to participate in the auction.

Cia de Investimentos Latinoamericana is a company created by Brazilian investment bank Banco Pactual to seek opportunities in the country's banking sector for investors, while Varejo is a unit of local Bozano Simonsen group, which owns investment bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen.

The investors that dropped out of the running are Credit Commerciale de France's Banco CCF do Brasil, General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corp, Banco Noroeste, BankBoston's Brazil unit and Tabal Participacoes.

A controlling stake in Credireal is due to be sold for at least 121.3 million reais at a closed-envelope auction at 1630 local/1930 GMT on the Minas Gerais-Espirito Santo-Brasilia Stock Exchange (BOVMESB).
However, the auction could face a delay if a lawsuit which was filed against the Credireal's privatization results in a court injunction blocking the sale.

According to the bank's tender documents, if the sealed bids are the same or within 10 percent of each other, investors will be required to continue bidding in a public auction beginning with the highest bid offered in the envelope.

Minas Gerais is selling a total of 986.6 million shares or 89.9 percent of Credireal's total capital at the auction as a 10 percent stake reserved to staff was fully acquired by bank employees, retirees and pension fund.
Credireal's staff was allowed to buy the stock at a 50 percent discount of the bank's minimum price which had been set at 130.8 million reais.
The Credireal sale follows the privatization of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, which was bought by Brazil's second top private bank Banco Itau .
Credireal, formally known as Banco de Credito Real de Minas Gerais SA, has a net worth of 98 million reais.
It posted a loss of 10.3 million reais or 9.87 reais per lot of 1,000 stock in the January-to-May period, according to the bank's latest published financial results.
The bank has 86 branches, of which 42 are in the southeastern state of Minas Gerais.
